commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing extends Deadline or Event, so the protected access on `from`,
`to`, and `by` gave no benefit; external code already goes through the
getters. Marking them final also documents that they are only ever set
in the constructor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set up Checkstyle and fix violations it found
commitResults.messageBody:
Adds the Gradle checkstyle plugin wired to AB3's checkstyle.xml/
suppressions.xml, which enforces the se-edu coding standard
automatically instead of relying on manual review.

Fixes the violations it caught on the existing codebase: six files
were missing a trailing newline, and three assertThrows lambdas in
ParserTest wrapped the line so that '(' started the continuation line
instead of ending the previous one; joining them onto one line (they
fit under 120 chars) resolves that.

`./gradlew checkstyleMain checkstyleTest` now passes with zero
violations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX GUI with a Spider-Man theme (Level 10)
commitResults.messageBody:
Follows Parts 1-4 of the se-edu JavaFX tutorial, built straight to the
Part 4 FXML architecture: Launcher/Main load MainWindow.fxml, which is
controlled by MainWindow and shows chat bubbles built by DialogBox.

Refactors Ui to return response strings instead of printing them
directly, and adds Peter#getResponse/getWelcomeMessage/getLoadingMessage/
isExit so the GUI and the existing CLI loop share one source of truth
for all chatbot text instead of duplicating message logic.

Themes the window with a red/blue/black palette, a subtle tiling
web-pattern background, and an original web-emblem avatar (radiating
spokes and rings) rather than any Marvel-owned character artwork.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adds TaskList(Task... tasks) so a list can be built from individual
tasks directly instead of wrapping them in List.of(...) first. Removes
the now-redundant no-arg constructor, since new TaskList() resolves
cleanly to the varargs constructor with zero elements.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix window to a non-resizable 400x600 to match the fixed anchor layout
commitResults.messageBody:
MainWindow.fxml positions its controls with fixed coordinates and
preferred sizes rather than fully responsive AnchorPane constraints, so
letting the user resize the window left empty space or clipped content.
Matches Part 2 of the JavaFX tutorial, which sets the same constraints.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams to replace manual loops over tasks (A-Streams)
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace hand-written for-loops that filter, transform, or collect over
a list of tasks with the equivalent Stream pipeline, where doing so
keeps or improves readability:

- TaskList.getTasksOnDate / findTasks: filter the task list with a
  predicate instead of manually building up a result list.
- Storage.load: map each saved line to a Task and drop the malformed
  ones (map + filter(Objects::nonNull)) instead of a loop with a
  null-check and manual add.
- Storage.save: map each task to its storage line instead of a loop
  that appends to a list.
- Ui.showTaskList / showFoundTasks: number and join each task's display
  line with IntStream + Collectors.joining instead of a StringBuilder
  loop.
- Ui.showTasksOnDate: prefix and join each task's display line with
  stream().map(...).collect(joining(...)) instead of a StringBuilder
  loop.

Each change is behaviour-preserving (verified by the existing
TaskListTest and ParserTest suites, which still pass) and was chosen
because the loop body was a straightforward filter/map/collect with no
mid-loop side effects beyond building the result - exactly the shape
Streams are meant for. Loops with genuine side effects elsewhere in the
codebase (e.g. Ui.readCommand, Storage.ensureDataFileExists) were left
alone, since forcing those into a Stream would trade a clear loop for
a stream used only for its side effects, which is discouraged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract addTaskAndRespond helper to remove duplication in handleCommand (A-CodeQuality)
commitResults.messageBody:
The TODO, DEADLINE, and EVENT cases in Peter.handleCommand each ended
with the exact same three statements: add the parsed task to the list,
persist the list to storage, and return the task-added confirmation
message. Introduce a private addTaskAndRespond(Task) helper that
performs this shared sequence once, and have each of the three cases
call it with their own parsed task instead.

This is the highest-priority issue found when reviewing the code
against the CS2103 code quality guidelines
(https://nus-cs2103-ay2627-s1.github.io/website/se-book-adapted/chapters/codeQuality.html):

- SLAP ("maintain a single level of abstraction"): the three cases
  mixed command-specific parsing with the generic add/persist/respond
  sequence in the same block. Each case now stays at one level by
  delegating the generic part to a named helper.
- Avoid Long Methods ("ideally under 30 lines"): handleCommand dropped
  from about 55 lines to about 40, closer to the guideline's target.

It also removes an implicit coupling: previously, changing the
add/persist/respond sequence meant remembering to update it in three
separate places; now there is a single place to change.

Verified with the existing ParserTest and TaskListTest suites (still
pass, since this only reshapes handleCommand without changing
behaviour) and Checkstyle (clean).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to document internal invariants (A-Assertions)
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `assert` statements at points where a violated condition would
indicate a programming bug rather than invalid user input (user input
is already validated and reported via PeterException, and stays that
way - assertions are not used as a substitute for that). Each one
documents an assumption the surrounding code already relies on:

- Task(String): the description passed in should never be null; every
  caller (Todo/Deadline/Event constructors, all fed by Parser after an
  emptiness check) already guarantees this.
- Command.fromKeyword(String): the keyword should never be null; its
  only caller, Parser.parseInput, always derives it from
  String.split(...)[0], which cannot return null.
- Parser.parseInput(String): rawInput should never be null; both the
  CLI (Ui.readCommand) and the GUI input path only ever pass a
  non-null line.
- TaskList(List<Task>): the loaded task list should never be null;
  its only caller passes Storage.load()'s result directly, which is
  documented to always return a (possibly empty) list.
- Event(String, LocalDateTime, LocalDateTime): the end time should not
  be before the start time. This documents an intended domain
  invariant; Parser.parseEvent does not yet enforce it on user input,
  so this also flags a gap to close later rather than a fully
  guaranteed precondition.
- Storage.createTask(String[], String): parts should have at least 3
  elements; its only caller, parseTask, already checks this before
  calling it, so the assertion documents that the two methods must be
  kept in sync.

Gradle's `test` task runs with assertions enabled by default, so these
are exercised on every test run; verified the existing ParserTest and
TaskListTest suites still pass with them in place, and Checkstyle is
clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
A-Assertions: document internal invariants with assert
A-CodeQuality: extract addTaskAndRespond to remove duplication
A-Streams: use Streams for task collection processing

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename `on` to `schedule` and order results as deadlines then events (BCD-Extension)
commitResults.messageBody:
Renames the date-lookup command from `on` to `schedule`, and changes
what it returns from an unordered mix of matching tasks to an actual
schedule: deadlines due that day first (sorted by due time), followed
by events starting that day (sorted by start time).

Why:
- `on <date>` answered "what's happening on this date" but the name
  didn't say so, and the result order was just insertion order (the
  order tasks were originally added), not the order they'd actually
  occur in - which is what you want from something calling itself a
  schedule.
- Grouping deadlines before events, each sorted chronologically within
  its group, is a deliberate, simple ordering rather than a single
  merge-by-time sort across both types: deadlines and events answer
  different questions ("due by" vs "happening from"), so keeping them
  visually separated avoids implying they're on one continuous
  timeline when a deadline's time isn't really a scheduled slot the
  way an event's is.

What changed:
- Command.ON -> Command.SCHEDULE.
- Peter.handleCommand's `case ON` -> `case SCHEDULE`, now calling the
  renamed TaskList/Ui methods below.
- TaskList.getTasksOnDate -> TaskList.getScheduleForDate: builds the
  deadline and event matches as two separately-sorted lists
  (Comparator.comparing(Deadline::getBy) /
  Comparator.comparing(Event::getFrom)) and concatenates them, instead
  of a single filter pass that preserved insertion order.
- Ui.showTasksOnDate -> Ui.showSchedule: message copy now talks about
  a "schedule" instead of what Peter "dug up".
- Parser's javadoc for parseDate updated to reference the `schedule`
  command instead of `on`.
- TaskListTest: renamed the existing tests to match, and added
  getScheduleForDate_multipleDeadlinesAndEvents_sortsEachGroupChronologically,
  since the original test only had one deadline and one event and so
  couldn't actually prove either the deadlines-before-events grouping
  or the within-group chronological order - both of which are the
  actual point of this change. Also strengthened the existing
  matching-deadline-and-event test to assert exact list equality
  (deadline then event) instead of just checking membership. Removed
  the now-unused assertFalse import.

Verified with the full test suite and Checkstyle (./gradlew check),
plus a manual run against a scratch data file (not the real
data/duke.txt): after adding a deadline and an event on the same date,
`schedule <date>` returned the deadline first, then the event, and
`on <date>` was correctly unrecognised.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merges the BCD-Extension increment: renames the `on <date>` command to
`schedule <date>`, and changes its result from an unordered mix of
matching tasks into an actual schedule - deadlines due that day first
(sorted by due time), followed by events starting that day (sorted by
start time).

See branch-BCD-Extension's commit (tagged BCD-Extension) for the full
rationale and list of changes.
